clue.text: Not in haste? Wrong, and (in short) on time (12, three words)

definitions.text: Not in haste? Wrong, and (in short) on time

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the preceding phrase must be rearranged

blocks.note: the phrase taken letter by letter
'n' is the short form of and, T the short form of time, and 'on' sets one beside the other

explanation.surface: Someone protests that being punctual does not mean being leisurely.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: ON THE INSTANT means immediately, so calling it 'not in haste' is wrong, and it is certainly on time. The added 'N and T join the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: On the instant means at once, without delay, which is the opposite of leisurely and squarely punctual.

clue.text: Native American house with a windmill sail inverted on top

indicators.note: in a down entry, inverted turns the letters upside down, so they read from bottom to top
in a down entry, on top puts the first piece above the house, so it comes first

blocks.note: taken as written
Chambers gives van as a windmill sail
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A Native American home topped by an upturned windmill sail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Navaho (also Navajo) are a Native American people of the south-western United States.

clue.text: Start of conflict interrupts actual respite

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: actual and true both mean real
the first letter of conflict

explanation.surface: A real lull is broken by the first shots of a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is a pause in fighting, a temporary relief or respite from hostilities.

clue.text: Greeting hairy man with regular cuts

indicators.note: cutting at regular intervals removes every other letter, leaving the alternate ones

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A hairy man getting a regular trim is greeted.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiya is an informal salutation, a contraction of 'how are you' used as hello.

clue.text: Sick with centre of meal trapped in part of intestine?

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, so only those are kept
something trapped is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: sick and ill are synonyms
the two middle letters of meal

explanation.surface: Someone is sick with half-digested food stuck in the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: Ileal means relating to the ileum, the final section of the small intestine, so it describes what is found there.

clue.text: The latest fashion unit representing some force

blocks.note: the latest thing is the new one
ton is an old word for the prevailing fashion

explanation.surface: The newest trend becomes a powerful force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ton' as fashion is from the French bon ton, high style.
explanation.definitionFit: The newton is the SI unit of force, enough to accelerate one kilogram by one metre per second squared.

clue.text: Water rising in gushing upset, precipitous as before

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards
gushing water is turbulent, so the word next to it is thrown into a new order
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: pee is slang for urine, a sort of water
the word itself, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Water rising in a gushing torrent makes a steep slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks an archaic word: steepe-up is Spenser's spelling for precipitous.
explanation.definitionFit: Steepe-up is an old compound meaning sheer or very steep, exactly what precipitous means.

clue.text: Finally fed with bit of entremets, possibly more (7, two words)

indicators.note: being fed with something means taking it inside, so one piece goes in the other
a bit of a word here is just its opening letter

blocks.note: at last means finally
the first letter of entremets

explanation.surface: At the end of a meal someone finally gets a morsel of dessert, and perhaps more.
explanation.walkthrough: Entremets is a French sweet course.
explanation.definitionFit: At least means no fewer than stated and possibly more, a minimum that could be exceeded.

clue.text: Education in Eton undergoing change must (6, two words)

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
something undergoing change is being altered, so the combined letters are reordered

blocks.note: ED is the abbreviation for education
taken as written

explanation.surface: Schooling at Eton must move with the times.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the famous English public (fee-paying) school.
explanation.definitionFit: Need to and must both express obligation, used before a verb in the same way.

clue.text: Like a snort? It's found in den on once retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a den and a lair are both animal homes
an is an obsolete form of on

explanation.surface: An animal snorts as it retreats into its den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Narial means relating to the nostrils, and a snort is a noise made through the nose, so a snort is narial.

clue.text: Old music maker creating minor misdeed in convent?

blocks.note: first meaning: a historical single-stringed bowed instrument
second meaning, whimsical: a small swindle perpetrated by the sisters

explanation.walkthrough: Fiddle is both a stringed instrument and a petty fraud, so the name of the old instrument also reads as a fraud by convent sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun's fiddle (tromba marina) is a medieval one-stringed bowed instrument, reputedly played in convents.

clue.text: Packs minimum of equipment in shorts

indicators.note: the minimum one can take of a word is its single opening letter
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: shorts are small measures of spirits, or tots
the first letter of equipment

explanation.surface: Someone travelling light packs almost nothing besides shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shorts' looks like clothing; here they are drinks of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry or lug, so totes means packs in the sense of carries along.

clue.text: Played, see, furiously? about end of match one's ready for bed

indicators.note: doing something furiously makes a wild mess, so the words before are jumbled
about means going round, so the jumble surrounds the other piece
the end of a word is its last letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the two words, to be rearranged
the last letter of match

explanation.surface: After a furious game, a player is worn out and ready for bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepyhead is a drowsy person, someone ready to go to sleep.

clue.text: Burrower clearly inside blind

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

blocks.note: to seel is to stitch shut a hawk's eyelids, blinding it
clearly and well both mean distinctly, as in seeing well

explanation.surface: A burrowing creature is evidently blind underground.
explanation.walkthrough: Seel is a falconry term, sewing up a young hawk's eyelids.
explanation.definitionFit: The sewellel, or mountain beaver, is a North American rodent that lives in underground tunnels.

clue.text: Brightly coloured fabric, reverse of worthless in brown

indicators.note: reverse of means everything that follows is read backwards
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: tan is a light brown
raca is a biblical term of contempt meaning worthless (Matthew 5:22)

explanation.surface: A gaudy fabric turns out cheap beneath its brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacarat is a bright orange-red colour, and also a fine linen or crape dyed that shade.

clue.text: God embraced by group coming together in prayer

indicators.note: being embraced means being held within, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a bee is a gathering of people, as in a sewing bee
D is an abbreviation for God (Latin Deus)

explanation.surface: A congregation gathers in prayer, wrapped in the presence of God.
explanation.definitionFit: Bede is an archaic word for a prayer, the root of bead, as in telling one's beads.

clue.text: Cast from Ibsen's Hedda

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, running across them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A reference to the cast of Ibsen's play Hedda Gabler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests actors in a play; it is the verb, as a snake casts its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to cast off or let fall, as a tree sheds leaves or an animal casts its coat.

clue.text: One bit of plush held by hatter I'm turned off, cosmetic (8, two words)

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the short word before it is read backwards
off means removed, so those letters are taken away
a bit of a word here is just its opening letter
held by means sitting inside, so these letters go within the other piece

blocks.note: a milliner makes and sells hats
taken as written
Roman numeral one
the first letter of plush

explanation.surface: A milliner abandons plush trimmings for make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing MI from the start of MILLINER leaves LLINER, which takes I and P after its first L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip liner is a cosmetic pencil used to outline the lips before applying lipstick.

clue.text: Duck pastry containing only half meat, dull

indicators.note: containing means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the pastry
only half keeps one half of the word, here its second two letters

blocks.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, O
a pie is a pastry dish
the last half of meat

explanation.surface: A disappointing duck pie with barely any meat in it, and dull besides.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck in cricket means a batsman's score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: To opiate is to dull or deaden, as an opium-based drug numbs pain.

clue.text: Before being taken in by dissembler, boss had no knowledge of this

definitions.text: boss had no knowledge of this

indicators.note: something taken in is absorbed within, so this piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: one who dissembles feigns, so is a feigner
or is an archaic word for before, as in 'or ever'

explanation.surface: A two-faced employee conceals a side job from the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' as OR is archaic, as in 'or ever'. The definition is a slang sense, not an outsider at all.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a foreigner is a private job done on the side, often with an employer's tools, without the boss knowing.

clue.text: Keep on about upcoming award in sonorous tones

indicators.note: in a down entry, upcoming means rising, so the letters read from the bottom upwards
about means going round, so the first piece surrounds the second

blocks.note: to rant is to keep on noisily
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A speaker drones on about an honour in a booming voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Reboant means resounding or loudly echoing, describing booming, sonorous sound.

clue.text: Sticker, ad scratched over in Bantu language

indicators.note: scratched means struck out, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: something that sticks is an adherer
taken as written, to be removed
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: An advertising sticker has been scratched off.
explanation.definitionFit: Herero is a Bantu language spoken in Namibia and Botswana by the Herero people.

clue.text: Copy U-turn travelling away from coastal region?

indicators.note: travelling letters move about, so the preceding words are rearranged

blocks.note: the two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver copies a U-turn while travelling inland.
explanation.definitionFit: Upcountry means in or towards the interior of a country, away from the coast.

clue.text: Cut bit of charcuterie up for burgers of a sort

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is just its opening letter
in a down entry, up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a cut of meat is a slice
the first letter of charcuterie

explanation.surface: Slicing cold cuts to make burgers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecils are fried balls of minced meat and breadcrumbs, a kind of rissole or burger.

clue.text: Poet penning number that's lingual in part

indicators.note: penning means shutting in, as in a pen, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: Kathleen Raine and Craig Raine are English poets
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A poet writing a number, a song with something lingual about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranine relates to the underside of the tongue, so it is lingual in one particular part.

clue.text: Feeble, old, and half dead with melancholy?

indicators.note: half keeps only one half of the word, here its opening two letters

blocks.note: the first half of dead
black bile was the humour thought to cause melancholy

explanation.surface: Someone old and frail is half dead with gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' tells you the definition is an archaic word; the question mark flags melancholy for bile, after the old theory of humours.
explanation.definitionFit: Debile is an obsolete word for weak or feeble, related to debility.

clue.text: Good film turned up relating to DNA?

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
cine is short for cinematographic film

explanation.surface: A good film about genetics comes to light.
explanation.definitionFit: Genic means relating to genes, which are made of DNA; the question mark admits the slight looseness.

clue.text: Foreign ruler experiences going round, capturing hearts

indicators.note: going round means turning back, so the word is read backwards
capturing means holding inside, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: to have is to experience
H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A foreign potentate tours his realm, winning hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Shah was the title of the monarch of Iran, a ruler from abroad from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Part of kit that's beaten, hand held (not half)

indicators.note: not half means losing half, so the second half of the word goes
held means kept inside, so the shortened word sits within the other

blocks.note: hit is a past participle meaning struck or beaten
taken as written, to be halved

explanation.surface: A drum held in the hand gets a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kit' here is a drum kit. 'That's beaten' looks like part of the definition, but beaten supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hi-hat is the pair of pedal-operated cymbals that forms part of a drum kit.

clue.text: Half getting submerged in Scotch mist

indicators.note: half means only one half survives, so the back part is dropped

blocks.note: someone drowning is getting submerged

explanation.surface: Half sunk in a damp Scottish drizzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch mist is the definition: drow is Scots for a drizzling mist or a cold squall.
explanation.definitionFit: Drow is a Scottish dialect word for a thick wet mist, the weather known as Scotch mist.

clue.text: Fawn-coloured wine sealed in wax

indicators.note: sealed in means shut inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: cere is an old word for wax, as in cerecloth
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A tawny wine in a bottle sealed with wax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fawn' suggests a colour; the definition plays on fawn as a young deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervine means deer-like and also describes a tawny deer colour, the shade of a fawn.

clue.text: Extract from travelogue, requirement for cyclist abroad

indicators.note: an extract is a passage lifted out, so the letters are found within the next word

blocks.note: the letters sit in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A travel writer notes what a cyclist needs on a foreign trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Vélo is the French word for a bicycle, the one thing a cyclist abroad needs.

clue.text: Scholarship giving one inclination to accept entry to Repton

indicators.note: the entry to a word is its first letter, so only that is taken
accepting means letting in, so one piece takes the other inside

blocks.note: a leaning is a tendency or inclination
the first letter of Repton

explanation.surface: A scholarship gives a pupil a taste for attending Repton.
explanation.walkthrough: Repton is an English public (fee-paying) school in Derbyshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning means erudition or acquired knowledge, which is what scholarship denotes.

clue.text: Wise, maybe? I can certainly pick winners

blocks.note: first meaning: comedian ... Wise, of Morecambe and Wise
second meaning: the machine that draws Premium Bond prizes

explanation.walkthrough: Wise looks like an adjective; it is a surname. Premium Bonds are a UK government savings scheme with a monthly prize draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise was a famous British comic, and ERNIE is the random number generator that selects Premium Bond winners.

clue.text: E.g. Clare lives with boy, name concealed

indicators.note: something concealed is hidden inside, so this letter goes within the boy

blocks.note: is means exists or lives
a lad is a boy
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A woman called Clare lives with a boy whose name is kept secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare looks like a woman's name; it is Clare Island off County Mayo, Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Clare Island is an island in Clew Bay, so it is an example of an island.

clue.text: Moped rotor comes loose, before being put back inside (12, two words)

indicators.note: parts coming loose fall out of place, so the preceding words are rearranged
put back means turned round, so the word is read backwards
inside places this piece within the jumbled letters

blocks.note: the two words, to be rearranged
to means before, as in ten to six

explanation.surface: A rotor works loose and has to be refitted on a moped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moped' looks like the past tense of mope; it is the small motorbike.
explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a light motorised two-wheeler, close kin to a motor scooter.
